context.title: The King Burns the Scroll
context.summary: Baruch writes Jeremiah's messages on a scroll and reads it publicly in the temple, and King Jehoiakim cuts it apart column by column and burns it. Jeremiah dictates the whole scroll again, with more added.
context.background: This happened in 605–604 BC. Scrolls were sheets of papyrus or leather joined in a long roll and written in columns, the 'leaves' of verse 23. A clay seal impression found in excavations in Jerusalem's City of David bears the name 'Gemaryahu son of Shaphan,' the official in whose room Baruch read the scroll (v. 10).

customs.note: Wealthy homes had warmer winter rooms heated by a brazier in the cold ninth month (about December). A 'penknife' was the scribe's knife for trimming reed pens.

watchFor: Josiah tore his clothes when the law was read (2 Kings 22:11); his son tears the scroll and 'they were not afraid' (v. 24).
Some officials beg him not to burn it (v. 25).
The word survives, with 'many like words' added (v. 32).

w: and he will cause to cease

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.summary: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599).

people.name: Baruch
people.summary: The secretary of the prophet Jeremiah (32:12; 36:4). He was of the tribe of Judah (51:59). To him Jeremiah dictated his prophecies regarding the invasion of the Babylonians and the Captivity.

people.name: Shaphan
people.summary: A coney, a scribe or secretary of king Josiah (2 Kings 22:3-7). He consulted Huldah concerning the newly-discovered copy of the law which was delivered to him by Hilkiah the priest (8-14).

people.name: Gemariah
people.summary: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror.

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: The son of Gemariah.

people.name: Elnathan
people.summary: Sent to find Uriah.

people.name: Delaiah
people.summary: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

people.name: Jehudi
people.summary: A Jew, son of Nethaniah.

people.name: Cushi
people.summary: Great-grandfather of Jehudi.

people.name: Hammelech
people.summary: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son.

people.name: Abdeel
people.summary: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

people.name: Azriel
people.summary: Esdra son of Solomon.

people.name: Jerahmeel
people.summary: Son of Hammelech (Jer. 36:26).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A son of the king, Seraiah.

people.name: Shelemiah
people.summary: Seraiah.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
